This looks like a problem in MSE buffering, not in the decoder. The first HEVC fragment plays, so the decoder works. comment:
Thanks for the clear test case.

**Analysis**

The `VideoFrame` constructor for an `ImageBitmap` ignores the alpha type of the bitmap, as the TODO in [VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1749) shows. Thus the frame treats the unpremultiplied pixels as premultiplied, and `drawImage` gives wrong colors.

This behavior does not agree with the spec. The [VideoFrame constructor](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-videoframe) makes the frame resource from "a copy of image's bitmap data". The [rendering rules](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-rendering) allow only color space conversion, crop, rotation and flip. None of these steps changes the alpha representation.

**Related bugs**

The patch on bug 1939711 (attachment 9652618) handles the crop and the alpha type of the `ImageBitmap` source in this constructor. That patch can fix this bug too. Bug 2079836 has the same color error for a `VideoFrame` from an RGBA buffer, with spec issue https://github.com/w3c/webcodecs/issues/972.

**Next steps**

Suggest that a person adds bug 1939711 as a dependency of this bug. Recommend that the attached test case becomes a test with that fix. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

comment:
The crash report and the code agree with the analysis in comment 0.

**Analysis**

The crash is on the main thread of a content process, on Nightly 160 and Windows 11, after 40 seconds of uptime. Frame 5 is the `ThenValue` of the lambda in `MediaDecoder::RequestDebugInfo` ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1648)).

`MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4744)) gives its promise `p` only to the runnable that it dispatches to `OwnerThread()`. If the dispatch fails, nothing settles `p`, and only a `MOZ_ASSERT` checks the result. The pending `FirstFrameLoaded` callback ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844)) is then destroyed without a result. The crash report has no browser shutdown annotations, so the cause of the dispatch failure is not known yet.

The check that crashes is in [MozPromise.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/xpcom/threads/MozPromise.h#541), under `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED`. Thus this crash occurs only in debug, Nightly and Developer Edition builds. In Release, the only effect is a lost `first_frame_loaded` telemetry record. The Release and ESR counts in comment 0 come from other `MozPromise` callers with the same signature.

**Regression**

Bug 1888265 (part 2 and part 5) added this `FirstFrameLoaded` call and the `MOZ_ASSERT`. We suggest that a developer sets `regressed_by` to bug 1888265.

**Next steps**

The bug has enough data to start a fix. :[person] already has an open needinfo from comment 0. No media meta bug matches this crash. The bug already blocks the Clouseau meta bug 1396527.

Thank you for the report and the xscreensaver log.

**Analysis**

This looks like a Linux regression in the wake lock code. In 2022, bug 1749187 stopped audio playback from inhibiting the screensaver. In Firefox 146, bug 1665986 added the "audio-playing" topic back to the wake lock listener for GTK. Its goal was to block system suspend during background audio.

Bug 1996504 then changed how the listener selects the inhibit type. Now an audio lock in the "locked-foreground" state becomes an idle inhibit, so the screensaver does not start. The relevant code is in [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1126). The "Playing audio" reason in your log matches this path.

The media element takes the audio lock in [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#5442). No pref controls this lock. Thus `media.video-wakelock` and `dom.screenwakelock.enabled` have no effect on it. Bug 1885268 tracks the request for a user control on screensaver inhibition.

**Next steps**

Bug 1996504 comment 8 says that the audio lock must block system suspend, but not dim prevention of the screen. Suggest that a developer confirms the regressor and sets `regressed_by` to bug 1665986 or bug 1996504. This bug now blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980.

comment:
Thank you for the clear test case.

**Analysis**

The `VideoFrame` constructor for an `ImageBitmap` ignores the alpha type of the bitmap. It wraps the surface from `ImageBitmap::ToCloneData()` and does not read `mAlphaType`, as the TODO in [VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1749) shows. Thus the frame uses unpremultiplied pixels as premultiplied pixels.

This behavior does not agree with the spec. The [WebCodecs spec](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-videoframe) says that the frame contains a copy of the bitmap data. [Rendering](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-rendering) only applies color space conversion, crop, rotation and flip. Thus `drawImage()` of the frame must give the same pixels as `drawImage()` of the bitmap.

Opaque pixels are not affected, because premultiplied and unpremultiplied values are equal at full alpha.

**Related bugs**

Bug 2079836 shows the same symptom for the RGBA buffer constructor. Bug 1939711 is about the crop rectangle in the same `ImageBitmap` path. As comment 2 says, the fix for the alpha type can also apply the crop. We suggest that the patch authors of the two bugs agree on one fix.

This bug now blocks bug 1746557, the WebCodecs meta bug.

**Next steps**

The attached test case is sufficient to start a fix. No more data is necessary.
title: VideoFrame created from an unpremultiplied ImageBitmap is drawn with wrong colors

The crash report confirms the analysis in comment 0.

**Analysis**

The crash is on the main thread of a content process, on Windows 11 with Nightly 160. Frame 5 is the `->Then()` lambda in `MediaDecoder::RequestDebugInfo` ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1662)). That lambda returns the promise from `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4744)). When the dispatch to the state machine task queue fails, that function ignores the error outside debug builds. Nothing resolves or rejects the returned promise, so the chained `FirstFrameLoaded` ThenValue dies without a result.

The crash comes from the check in `ThenValueBase::AssertIsDead` ([MozPromise.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/xpcom/threads/MozPromise.h#543)). This check runs only when `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED` is set, thus release builds do not crash. In release builds, Firefox only skips the `first_frame_loaded` telemetry for that load. Crash-stats shows 159 crashes with this crash reason since 2026-04-13, all in content processes on Nightly, DevEdition and Beta. Other MozPromise crashes share this signature, so the release counts in comment 0 come from different causes.

Bug 1888265 added the `RequestDebugInfo` call in `MediaDecoder::FirstFrameLoaded` ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844)). The `FirstFrameLoaded` call site in the crash reason did not exist before that change. Bug 1896281 tracked the same crash reason in CI. Bug 1899996 tracked the related `MOZ_ASSERT` failure in `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo`. A bot closed both bugs as incomplete, and no fix landed.

**Next steps**

The data on this bug is sufficient to start a fix. We recommend the direction in comment 0: reject `p` when `OwnerThread()->Dispatch` fails.

Thank you for the clear steps and the workaround details.

**Analysis**

This looks like a gap in the Firefox audio output path, not a site problem. When playback starts with no output device, the audio stream fails to open. For the default device, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#676) then rejects its ended promise. The code schedules a retry only when the page selects a device with `setSinkId()`. That retry came from bug 1829054. A stream error during playback ends in the same rejection, at [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#759).

After the rejection, [`NeedAudioSink()`](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#461) stays false, so pause and resume do not open a new audio stream. [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4675) marks the audio as complete and continues the video on the system clock. A seek stops and starts the media sink again, so the audio comes back. No code reacts when a new default device appears.

**Fix direction**

When the default device fails and the media has video, call `ScheduleRetrySink()` instead of the rejection. Keep the rejection for audio-only media, so that the element still reports the error. Another option is to retry only when cubeb reports a change in the device list. This prevents a stream open every second on a computer with no audio device.

The analysis assumes that the WASAPI stream open fails when Windows has no output device. Both failure paths end in the same rejection, so the conclusion does not change.

**Next steps**

The next step is a fix in `AudioSinkWrapper`. This bug now blocks the Bluetooth meta bug 2011679.

Until a fix lands, seek in the video or reload the tab to restore the audio.

comment:
The analysis in comment 0 is correct for the current code.

**Analysis**

`MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` creates the promise `p` and dispatches a runnable that resolves it ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4752)). If the dispatch to the owner `TaskQueue` fails, the runnable is destroyed. Only a debug `MOZ_ASSERT` checks `rv`, and the function returns `p` unsettled.

The reader's `Then` callback in [MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1666) returns that `p`, so its completion promise chains onto `p`. When the last reference to `p` drops, `AssertIsDead` finds the pending `FirstFrameLoaded` callback from [MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844) and crashes.

The crash comes from code in [MozPromise.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/xpcom/threads/MozPromise.h#543) under `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED`. Thus it crashes the content process only in Nightly, DevEdition and debug builds. In release builds, the promise is destroyed without a crash, and the first-frame telemetry probe is lost.

The crash report shows a content process on Windows 11, Nightly 160, with an uptime of 40 seconds. It has no shutdown annotations. It is not known why the `TaskQueue` refuses the dispatch while `mShuttingDown` is still false.

Bug 1888265 ([00865b70298e](https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/00865b70298e)) changed the check on `rv` from `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT` to `MOZ_ASSERT`. Before that change, a failed dispatch crashed at the dispatch site. The missing reject is older than that change. Bug 1896281 tracked the same crash reason as an intermittent test failure.

**Next steps**

Suggested fix: when `OwnerThread()->Dispatch` fails, return `GenericPromise::CreateAndReject(rv, __func__)` or reject `p`. The `FirstFrameLoaded` callback already handles a reject. Also update `HTMLMediaElement::MozRequestDebugInfo`, which has `MOZ_ASSERT_UNREACHABLE` on a reject ([HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#2408)). The existing `mShuttingDown` reject can already reach that assert.

Thanks for the test case and the analysis.

**Analysis**

The cause is in the `VideoFrame` constructor that takes an `ImageBitmap`. It wraps the raw `data->mSurface` from `ImageBitmap::ToCloneData()` and ignores `data->mAlphaType` ([VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1749)). The draw path then marks every RGBA and BGRA frame as premultiplied ([nsLayoutUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/layout/base/nsLayoutUtils.cpp#7192)). Thus the canvas unpremultiplies straight alpha pixels, and the color values overflow.

The WebCodecs spec says that the frame holds a copy of the bitmap data ([VideoFrame constructor](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-videoframe)). Rendering can change only the color space, crop, rotation and flip ([Rendering](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-rendering)). Thus `drawImage(frame)` must give the same pixels as `drawImage(bitmap)`.

This is not a regression. The TODO comes from the first implementation in bug 1774300. Bug 2079836 shows the same symptom for frames from RGBA buffers. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

**Next steps**

The patch on bug 1939711 (D330607) handles both the crop and the alpha type in this constructor. Thus it can also fix this bug. The fix direction: premultiply the surface when `mAlphaType` is `NonPremult`, before the constructor wraps it. We recommend that the patches for bug 1939711 and bug 2079836 use one approach to alpha.

Thomas, could you please check if D330607 makes the attached test case pass? If it does, we can add the test case to that patch and close this bug with it.
title: VideoFrame created from an unpremultiplied ImageBitmap is drawn with wrong colors

Thank you for the xscreensaver log.

**Analysis**

On Linux, a foreground `audio-playing` wake lock now inhibits the screensaver. In [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1126), `WakeLockListener::Callback` sends a "locked-foreground" audio lock to a foreground topic. A foreground topic uses an idle inhibitor: the portal IDLE flag, the GNOME IDLE flag, or `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` `Inhibit` with the reason "Playing audio" ([WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#580)). This matches your xscreensaver-systemd log.

The media element takes the `audio-playing` lock in [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#5442). None of the three prefs that you set control this lock. On macOS and Windows, the audio lock only prevents system sleep and does not keep the display on ([nsAppShell.mm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/widget/cocoa/nsAppShell.mm#82), [nsAppShell.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/widget/windows/nsAppShell.cpp#81)).

This is a regression from bug 1996504, which shipped in Firefox 146. Before it, bug 1665986 added the `audio-playing` topic back to the GTK listener with only a suspend inhibitor. Bug 1996504 made the foreground or background choice depend only on the lock state. Thus foreground audio got an idle inhibitor again. Bug 1749187 removed this behavior in 2022 for the same reason as this bug.

**Next steps**

The cause is in the GTK widget code, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk. A possible fix: in `WakeLockListener::Callback`, always send `audio-playing` to the background topic, which takes only a suspend inhibitor. The `download-in-progress` topic probably needs the same change. This bug blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980. Bug 2074999 also reports a blocked xscreensaver on Linux, but its cause is not clear yet.

comment:
Thank you for the test page and the clear narrowing.

**Analysis**

After `fastSeek()`, the audio starts one WebM cluster before the video keyframe. In the attached clip, this is 2 seconds. Two steps cause this together:

1. For a fast seek, the audio seek target is the time where the video seek landed ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3200)). This is a keyframe at a cluster start. `WebMDemuxer::SeekInternal` subtracts the Opus seek preroll (80 ms) from the target before the cue lookup ([WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1172)). Thus the audio seek finds the previous cluster.
2. In a fast seek, `AccurateSeekingState::HandleAudioDecoded` pushes the first audio sample with no trim ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1822)). Only the accurate seek drops audio up to the target, in `DropAudioUpToSeekTarget`. The clock starts at the keyframe, so the audio stays behind the video.

This agrees with each case that you tested. Vorbis and MP4 have no seek preroll. Setting `currentTime` does an accurate seek. A seek to the first keyframe clamps to the start time. Your `fastSeek(3.9)` case lands before the old position, so `AdjustFastSeekIfNeeded` changes it to an accurate seek.

**Next steps**

The suggested fix is to drop and trim the audio up to the video keyframe time in a fast seek. This can reuse `DropAudioUpToSeekTarget` with the keyframe time as the target. A second change can apply the seek preroll to the audio track only. A WebM and Opus mochitest can cover this. We need no more data from you.
title: Audio out of sync with video after fastSeek() on a WebM with Opus audio

Thank you for the detailed report and the ffmpeg commands.

**Analysis**

The cause seems to be two code paths that act together. The fix from bug 2026875 works: the parser reads the audio `tfdt` correctly as -1008.

1. `MP4TrackDemuxer::GetNextSample` moves an audio sample with a negative start time to 0 and makes its duration almost 0 ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#531)). The decode time does not change.
2. `TrackBuffersManager::ProcessFrames` then uses this short duration as the longest frame duration ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2286)). The next audio sample starts about 21 ms later, so MSE detects a discontinuity ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2124)). The discontinuity resets all tracks, and the video track then needs a keyframe.
3. On macOS, the demuxer marks an HEVC sample as a keyframe only when it is an IDR frame ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#479)). Bug 2049615 added this check for seeking. x265 uses open GOP by default, so segment 1 starts with a CRA frame. MSE drops all video samples in segment 1, and the buffered range stops at 5.875 s.

This also explains the H.264 result: its segment 1 starts with an IDR frame. The `make_zero` stream plays because the demuxer does not shorten any audio sample.

This analysis comes from the code only. Nobody has confirmed it with a log or a build yet. Our tools cannot open the zip attachment, but the ffmpeg commands in comment 0 are sufficient to make a test stream. Bug 2017567 is related work on time overflow in MSE.

**Next steps**

We can fix this in one of two places, or in both:

- Do not let a trimmed audio sample set the longest frame duration for the discontinuity check.
- Apply the IDR-only HEVC rule on seek only, or let MSE accept a CRA frame as a random access point.

Paul, could you please confirm this cause? You made the change in bug 2049615.
title: HLS fMP4 with HEVC video stalls at the end of the first segment when the audio track's decode time starts negative (tfdt stored as 2^64−N)

Thank you for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

This bug has a clear cause. When the default output device is not available, Firefox stops the audio of the playing element. It does not try to open the audio again later.

- When the audio stream does not open on the default device, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#669) rejects the audio "ended" promise. It schedules a retry only for a device that the page selected with `setSinkId()`.
- The same rule applies when the async start fails ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#569)) and when the stream fails after it starts ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#754)).
- [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4675) then marks the audio as complete. The video continues on the system clock, without audio.
- A resume does not make a new audio sink, because `NeedAudioSink()` stays false. A seek stops and starts the media sink again, so the audio comes back.

Bug 1829054 added the retry for `setSinkId()` devices only. This is not a regression, because the default device never had a retry.

**Next steps**

A possible fix: for media with video, keep the audio sink of the default device pending and retry it, as the `setSinkId()` path does. Audio-only media can keep the current error. This bug now blocks the Bluetooth meta bug 2011679.

Until a fix lands, seek or reload the tab to get the audio back.

comment:
This crash comes from a promise in `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` that nothing settles. The analysis in comment 0 matches the current code.

**Analysis**

`MediaDecoder::FirstFrameLoaded` requests debug info for telemetry and chains a `FirstFrameLoaded` callback on the result ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844)). After the reader step, `MediaDecoder::RequestDebugInfo` returns the promise from the state machine ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1666)).

`MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` gives its `GenericPromise::Private` to a runnable for the state machine task queue ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4744)). When `Dispatch` fails, the task queue destroys the runnable. The code checks `rv` only with `MOZ_ASSERT` and returns the unsettled promise. When the last reference goes, `AssertIsDead` finds the pending `FirstFrameLoaded` callback and crashes. The crash reason "dispatchRv: not dispatched" and frames 0 to 6 match this path.

The check that crashes exists only when `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT_ENABLED` is set, which is Nightly, Developer Edition and debug builds ([MozPromise.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/xpcom/threads/MozPromise.h#30)). In the last 30 days, 21 crashes have this crash reason. All of them are on Nightly and Developer Edition, on Windows and macOS. The release and ESR counts in comment 0 are for the same generic signature, but they have other causes. In release builds, this path loses one telemetry sample and does not crash.

One point is not proven: why the dispatch fails while `mShuttingDown` is still false. A possible trigger is the thread pool that refuses work at XPCOM shutdown, but the crash data does not confirm it.

**Related bugs**

Bug 1888265 (Firefox 126) added the `FirstFrameLoaded` to `RequestDebugInfo` chain. The same bug changed the dispatch check from `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT` to `MOZ_ASSERT`, so the failure now shows as this promise crash. Bug 1896281 shows the same crash reason in `test_DifferentStreamStartTimes.html`. BugBot closed it as an inactive intermittent.

**Next steps**

Suggested fix direction:

1. In `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo`, reject `p` with `rv` when `Dispatch` fails. The `FirstFrameLoaded` callback already handles a rejection.
2. Check `MediaFormatReader::RequestDebugInfo` for the same problem ([MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/64cfaf34e56f4c82eea77d032ec592c083b5b161/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3437)). It uses `InvokeAsync`, which does not settle its promise when the dispatch fails.
3. As an option, keep the `FirstFrameLoaded` request in a `MozPromiseRequestHolder` and disconnect it in `MediaDecoder::Shutdown`.

2. For Opus, `WebMDemuxer::SeekInternal` subtracts the 80 ms SeekPreRoll from the target ([WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1182)). It seeks with the cues of the video track ([WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1165)). Thus the target of 5.92 s lands on the cue at 4.0 s.
3. On a fast seek, `AccurateSeekingState` pushes the first audio sample as it is ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1823)). Only an accurate seek calls `DropAudioUpToSeekTarget`. The playback position becomes 6.0 s, so the audio from 4.0 s plays about 2 seconds late.

The variants in comment 0 agree with this cause. Vorbis has no SeekPreRoll, so its audio lands on the 6.0 s cue. A `currentTime` seek is accurate and drops the early audio. For `fastSeek(3.9)` from 1 s, the audio lands at 0 s, before the old position. Then `AdjustFastSeekIfNeeded` changes the seek to an accurate seek ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#2064)).

This case is related to bug 1188313 (A/V sync after a fast seek) and bug 945863 (Opus SeekPreRoll in WebM). Both bugs are fixed.

**Next steps**

The suggested fix: on a fast seek, drop the decoded audio before the time where the video seek landed. Keep the SeekPreRoll, because the Opus decoder needs that audio. Another option is to not subtract the SeekPreRoll when the seek uses the video cues. No action is necessary from you.
title: Audio out of sync with video after fastSeek() on a WebM with Opus audio

This is a defect in the `VideoFrame` constructor that takes an `ImageBitmap`. Bug 1774300 added this constructor without alpha handling, so this is not a regression.

**Analysis**

`ImageBitmap::ToCloneData()` returns the raw surface. The crop and the alpha state are in separate fields, `mPictureRect` and `mAlphaType`. The constructor wraps only `data->mSurface` and ignores both fields, at the existing TODO in [VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1750).

When the bitmap itself is drawn, `PrepareForDrawTarget` premultiplies `NonPremult` data in [ImageBitmap.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/canvas/ImageBitmap.cpp#827). Thus the direct draw is correct.

When the frame is drawn, `SurfaceFromVideoFrame` marks every RGBA and BGRA frame as premultiplied in [nsLayoutUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/layout/base/nsLayoutUtils.cpp#7193). The unpremultiply step then overflows and gives the `(142, 199, 99, 128)` readback.

**Fix direction**

The fix belongs in the same constructor as bug 1939711, which loses `mPictureRect`. Its patch (attachment 9652618) says that it handles the crop and the alpha type together. Bug 2079836 adds alpha tracking and a premultiplied draw cache for the buffer path. That mechanism can also carry `NonPremult` from an `ImageBitmap`. We recommend that the two patches agree on one place to handle alpha.

The value that `copyTo()` must return for this source is still open in https://github.com/w3c/webcodecs/issues/972.

**Next steps**

We suggest that a developer makes this bug depend on bug 1939711. If that patch lands with a test for this case, this bug can close as a duplicate. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.
title: VideoFrame created from an unpremultiplied ImageBitmap is drawn with wrong colors

Thank you for the synthetic reproducer and the control stream.

**Analysis**

The triage tools cannot open zip attachments. This analysis uses the commands and the log lines in comment 0. It comes from the code only, and nobody has run the stream yet.

Two problems combine, and only in macOS builds (`MOZ_APPLEMEDIA`):

1. **A false discontinuity in the audio track.** [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#531) moves the negative start of the first AAC frame to 0. This makes the frame about 0.33 ms long. [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2286) then uses this short value as `mLongestFrameDuration`. The second frame starts about 21 ms later, so the check at [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2124) detects a discontinuity. This calls `ResetAppendState()` on all tracks, and sets "need random access point" on the video track too. The video of segment 0 is already processed at this time, so the video track starts segment 1 with the flag set.
2. **On macOS, HEVC CRA frames are not keyframes.** Since bug 2049615, [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#479) accepts only IDR frames as keyframes. x265 uses open GOP by default, so segment 1 probably has CRA frames and no IDR frame. Thus [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2038) drops every video frame of segment 1. `buffered` is the intersection of the audio and video ranges, so it stays at `[0, 5.875]`.

This agrees with the table in comment 0. x264 uses closed GOP, so segment 1 starts on an IDR frame and the flag clears at once. The `make_zero` control does not trim the first audio frame, so no false discontinuity occurs.

**Related bugs**

Bug 2065822 reports the same CRA problem for MSE on macOS, and bug 2049615 also caused it. The patch on bug 2065822 makes every IRAP frame a keyframe, and that also unblocks this stream. This bug stays open for the first problem: a trimmed pre-roll frame must not cause a false discontinuity. Bug 2026875 did not cause this. It only lets the negative decode time reach the older trimming code.

**Next steps**

For the discontinuity, the suggested fix is in `ProcessFrames`. Use the full frame duration (`mOriginalPresentationWindow` when it is set) for `mLongestFrameDuration` and `mLastFrameDuration`. Windows and Linux are probably not affected, because the CRA rule exists only in macOS builds. We suggest that a person with edit rights sets the OS field to macOS. Nothing more is necessary from the reporter.

Thank you for the clear test case and the variations.

**Analysis**

This looks like an interaction between the fast seek path and the Opus seek preroll in the WebM demuxer. The analysis below comes from a code read. No log confirms it yet.

1. On a fast seek, the video seeks first to the keyframe K. Then [MediaFormatReader.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaFormatReader.cpp#3196) sets the audio seek time to K.
2. `WebMDemuxer::SeekInternal` uses the video cues and subtracts `mSeekPreroll` from the target. Opus sets 80 ms, and Vorbis sets 0. See [WebMDemuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webm/WebMDemuxer.cpp#1165).
3. The cue lookup for K minus 80 ms finds the keyframe before K. Thus the audio starts about one keyframe interval too early.
4. A fast seek pushes the first audio sample with no trim. Only an accurate seek calls `DropAudioUpToSeekTarget`. See [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#1820).
5. The audio clock then plays the early audio as if it starts at K. The audio stays behind the video.

This agrees with each of your variations. A `currentTime` seek trims the audio. Vorbis has no preroll, and MP4 uses a different demuxer. A seek to the first keyframe clamps to the start time. The short forward seek becomes an accurate seek in `AdjustFastSeekIfNeeded`.

**Next steps**

A suggested fix is to trim the decoded audio up to K in the fast seek path. The trim must come after the decoder, so that the Opus decoder still gets its preroll. Another option is to apply the preroll only to the audio cue lookup in `WebMDemuxer::SeekInternal`. A mochitest with this test case can cover the fix. No action is necessary from you at this time.

The root cause in comment 0 is correct, and the spec agrees that this is a Firefox bug.

**Analysis**

The `ImageBitmap` constructor in [VideoFrame.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webcodecs/VideoFrame.cpp#1749) wraps only `data->mSurface` from `ImageBitmap::ToCloneData()`. It ignores `mAlphaType` and `mPictureRect`, which [ImageBitmap.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/canvas/ImageBitmap.cpp#975) already fills in.

At draw time, `nsLayoutUtils::SurfaceFromVideoFrame` always sets `gfxAlphaType::Premult` in [nsLayoutUtils.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/layout/base/nsLayoutUtils.cpp#7193). Thus the canvas unpremultiplies the straight alpha pixels a second time, and the values overflow. Drawing the `ImageBitmap` directly works because `ImageBitmap::PrepareForDrawTarget` crops to `mPictureRect` and premultiplies `NonPremult` data.

The [VideoFrame constructor](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-videoframe) makes a media resource with "a copy of image's bitmap data". [VideoFrame rendering](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-rendering) adds only color space conversion, crop, rotation and flip. Thus the frame must draw with the same colors as the bitmap.

**Related work**

Bug 1939711 (crop) drops its data at the same lines. Its open patch, [D330607](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D330607), has the title "Handle ImageBitmap source's crop and alpha type in VideoFrame constructor". Bug 2079836 fixes the RGBA buffer constructor and also changes the draw-side alpha handling.

**Next steps**

Suggest a test of D330607 with the attached testcase. If D330607 fixes it, we can close this bug as a duplicate of bug 1939711. Make sure that D330607 and the bug 2079836 patch do not both premultiply the same pixels. This bug now blocks the WebCodecs meta bug 1746557.

Thank you for the report and the xscreensaver log.

**Analysis**

This is a regression on Linux. Bug 1749187 stopped the screensaver inhibit for audio in Firefox 107. Bug 1665986 in Firefox 146 added the "audio-playing" wake lock back, but only as a suspend inhibitor.

Bug 1996504, also in Firefox 146, changed how [WakeLockListener.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/widget/gtk/WakeLockListener.cpp#1126) selects the inhibitor. It now uses only the lock state. A visible tab sends "locked-foreground", so its "audio-playing" lock takes the idle inhibitor. This is the `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` call with the "Playing audio" reason in your log.

No pref turns off the "audio-playing" wake lock. [HTMLMediaElement.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediaelement/HTMLMediaElement.cpp#5442) and [AudioDestinationNode.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webaudio/AudioDestinationNode.cpp#773) do not check a pref before they create it. The three prefs in comment 0 apply only to video and to the Screen Wake Lock API.

On Windows and macOS, the "audio-playing" lock only prevents system sleep ([nsAppShell.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/widget/windows/nsAppShell.cpp#81), [nsAppShell.mm](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/widget/cocoa/nsAppShell.mm#82)). It does not stop the screensaver.

**Next steps**

The code at fault is in widget/gtk, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk. A suggested fix: in `WakeLockListener::Callback`, send every "audio-playing" lock to the suspend-only inhibitor. This keeps the suspend inhibit from bug 1665986 for background audio. A foreground "download-in-progress" lock possibly has the same problem.

Martin, could you please look at this regression from bug 1996504?

This bug blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980. Bug 1885268 is related: it asks for a user control for the video screensaver inhibit.

comment:
The analysis in comment 0 is correct. `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` can return a promise that nothing settles.

**Analysis**

`MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo` creates a `GenericPromise::Private` and dispatches a runnable that resolves it ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4751)). When the state machine `TaskQueue` is already shut down, the dispatch fails with `NS_ERROR_ILLEGAL_DURING_SHUTDOWN` and the queue deletes the runnable. Only a debug `MOZ_ASSERT` checks the result, and the function returns the pending promise ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4760)). The `FirstFrameLoaded` telemetry `Then()` waits on this promise ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#844)). When the last reference drops, `MozPromise` finds the pending `ThenValue` and crashes. The crash stack and the reason "dispatchRv: not dispatched" match this chain.

Bug 1888265 added the `FirstFrameLoaded` `Then()` in Firefox 126. Thus this crash is a regression from that bug. The check that crashes is a `MOZ_DIAGNOSTIC_ASSERT`. Thus the crash occurs only in Nightly, Developer Edition and debug builds. The release and ESR counts in comment 0 are different crashes with the same generic signature. All recent crash reports with the `FirstFrameLoaded` reason come from the content process, on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Bug 1896281 and bug 1899996 show the same failure in CI tests. Both bugs closed as INCOMPLETE without a fix. Suggest adding them to "See Also".

**Next steps**

The recommended fix is in `MediaDecoderStateMachine::RequestDebugInfo`: when `OwnerThread()->Dispatch` fails, reject `p` with `rv`. The `FirstFrameLoaded` callback already handles a rejection. As an option, the lambda in `MediaDecoder::RequestDebugInfo` can return a rejected promise after shutdown ([MediaDecoder.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoder.cpp#1660)). `MediaSource` calls the same function, and the fix also protects that caller ([MediaSource.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/MediaSource.cpp#682)).
title: Crash in [@ mozilla::MozPromise<T>::ThenValue<T>::DoResolveOrRejectInternal]

The code at fault is in widget/gtk, so this bug moves to Core :: Widget: Gtk. The bug also blocks the wake lock meta bug 1665980.

Thank you for the synthetic stream and the clear steps.

**Analysis**

This looks like two faults in the MSE path that combine. The `tfdt` change from bug 2026875 works and reads the audio start as -1008. This cause comes from a code review only. No media log confirms it yet.

1. The demuxer moves the first AAC sample with a negative time to 0 and makes its duration very short ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#514)). It does not change the decode timestamp of the sample.
2. MSE then uses this short duration as the longest frame duration. The next audio frame looks like a gap, and `TrackBuffersManager` reports a discontinuity ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2124)).
3. The discontinuity sets the "need random access point" flag on all tracks, also on the video track ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2153)).
4. On macOS, the demuxer marks an HEVC frame as a keyframe only if it is an IDR frame ([MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#475)). This rule came from bug 2049615. By default, x265 makes open GOP streams, so the second segment starts with a CRA frame. MSE then drops all later video frames ([TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2038)), and `buffered` stays at the end of the first segment.

This explains your table. x264 makes closed GOP streams, so each segment starts with an IDR frame and the video track recovers. The `make_zero` control has no negative time, so no false discontinuity occurs. The IDR rule applies only to macOS builds, so Windows and Linux probably do not show this stall.

**Next steps**

Suggested fix direction:

1. When the demuxer moves a negative audio time to 0, also adjust the decode timestamp. As an alternative, skip this change for MSE.
2. Accept a CRA frame as a random access point for MSE buffering. Use the IDR rule only where the decoder starts after a seek.

A developer can confirm the cause with `MOZ_LOG=MediaSource:5,MediaSourceSamples:5` and the stream from comment 0. The log must show "Discontinuity detected" in the first segment, then "skipping sample" for the video frames of the second segment. comment:
Thank you for the clear report.

**Analysis**

This looks like a known Bluetooth problem. When you pause, Firefox stops the audio output. When the output starts again, the headphones or the macOS Bluetooth route probably fade the audio in. Firefox has no fade code in its audio sink.

On a regular pause, Firefox stops the cubeb stream. Only a seek pause keeps the stream running ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#356)). The stop calls `cubeb_stream_stop` ([AudioStream.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/AudioStream.cpp#433)), and the macOS backend then stops the output unit ([mod.rs](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/third_party/rust/cubeb-coreaudio/src/backend/mod.rs#1299)). After a pause longer than `media.dormant-on-pause-timeout-ms` (5000 ms), Firefox also destroys the stream and creates a new one on resume.

Bug 2055266 reported the same symptom on Windows. Bug 2059525 tracks stream reuse on seek for all platforms. That pref is already on for macOS, but it does not cover a regular pause. This bug is the pause case.

**Next steps**

A possible fix is to keep the stream running and write silence for a short time after a pause. After that time, Firefox can stop the stream. The fix must also cover the resume from the dormant state. The cost is more CPU and power use while the video is paused.

This bug now blocks bug 2011679, the meta bug for Bluetooth audio problems. You do not need to do anything now.

Thank you for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

This looks like a gap in the retry logic of [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#669). When the audio sink cannot open, the code schedules a retry only for a device that the page chose with `setSinkId()`. For the default output device, `SyncCreateAudioSink()` and [`OnAudioEnded()`](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#754) reject `mEndedPromiseHolder` and stop. After this, [`NeedAudioSink()`](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#461) stays false. Thus the retry in `GetPosition()` and the sink start in `SetPlaying(true)` never run. Because the media has a video track, `OnMediaSinkAudioError()` in [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4690) lets the video continue without audio.

This matches the reported behavior. A pause and resume goes through `SetPlaying(true)`, so the audio does not come back. A seek or a reload calls `Start()` again, and `Start()` creates a new audio sink. A pause of more than 5 seconds probably makes the player go dormant, and the resume is then a seek. This can explain why a pause before the connection helps.

**Next step**

A possible fix: when the default device fails and the media has video, schedule a retry and keep the ended promise pending. Apply this to all three failure paths. The existing poll in `GetPosition()` then creates the audio sink again after the device appears. Audio-only media must still report the error. The retry logic came from bug 1829054, and it covers only devices that the page chose with `setSinkId()`.

This bug now blocks bug 2011679, the meta bug for Bluetooth device audio and video. The steps are sufficient for a developer to reproduce the problem.

comment:
Thank you for the clear reproducer. Our tools cannot read archives, so we did not open the zip attachment. This analysis comes from the bug text and the code.

**Analysis**

Two defects combine to cause the stall. Both are in the MSE path, and the second one occurs only on macOS.

1. The first AAC frame starts at -1008/48000 s. [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#514) moves its start time to 0 and cuts its duration to 16/48000 s. The bug 2026875 fix reads the `tfdt` correctly, so that fix is not the cause.
2. [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2286) uses this short duration as the longest frame duration of the audio track. The gap to the next audio frame is more than two times that value. Thus the discontinuity check in [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2124) fires on a continuous stream. It sets the "need random access point" flag on all tracks, and the video track is one of them.
3. On macOS, [MP4Demuxer.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mp4/MP4Demuxer.cpp#476) marks an HEVC sample as a keyframe only when it is an IDR picture. By default, x265 makes open GOP streams, so the second segment probably starts on a CRA picture. Then [TrackBuffersManager.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasource/TrackBuffersManager.cpp#2038) drops every video frame of that segment and reports no error.

The `buffered` range is the intersection of the tracks, so it stays at the end of the first segment. This also explains your controls. With `make_zero`, no audio start time is negative, so no false discontinuity occurs. x264 makes closed GOP streams, so the H.264 segment starts on an IDR picture and clears the flag. We expect this stream to play on Windows and Linux, because there the CRA picture keeps its sync flag. We did not test this.

Step 3 is the same defect as bug 2065822. Bug 2049615 added that IDR check in Firefox 154, so we mark it as the regressor. Step 2 is a separate defect, and it stays after bug 2065822 is fixed.

**Next steps**

The suggested fix has two parts:

1. Fix bug 2065822: treat every HEVC IRAP picture (CRA, BLA) as a random access point in `MP4Demuxer`. Handle the VideoToolbox RASL limit in `AppleVTDecoder`.
2. In `TrackBuffersManager::ProcessFrames`, use the untrimmed frame duration for the gap check. The `mOriginalPresentationWindow` field holds it when the demuxer trims a frame.

A release build gives no signal when MSE drops all frames of a segment. A console warning can help pages find this problem. We suggest that a developer adds a dependency on bug 2065822. A `MediaSource:5` log of the reproducer can confirm the chain. Look for "Discontinuity detected" in the first segment, then "skipping sample" for the video of the second segment.
title: HLS fMP4 with HEVC video stalls at the end of the first segment when the audio track's decode time starts negative (tfdt stored as 2^64−N)

Thanks for the clear report and the tests you did.

**Analysis**

When you pause a video, Firefox stops the audio output stream. When you play again, Firefox starts the stream again. Some Bluetooth headphones go to sleep when the output stops, so the audio can fade in after the restart.

Firefox keeps the stream running only for a seek, with `media.audio.reuse-stream-on-seek` (bug 2052692). This pref is on by default on macOS. comment:
Thank you for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

The code in [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#654) explains the silent tab.

1. When playback starts with no output device, `AudioSinkWrapper::SyncCreateAudioSink` fails to open the audio stream. No `setSinkId()` device is set, so it rejects `mEndedPromiseHolder` and schedules no retry ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#676)). The async path does the same ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#576)).
2. `MediaDecoderStateMachine::OnMediaSinkAudioError` continues the playback because the media has video ([MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4675)). The clock then uses the system time, and the audio data is dropped.
3. The periodic retry in `AudioSinkWrapper::GetPosition` runs only when `NeedAudioSink()` is true ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#211)). After the rejection, `NeedAudioSink()` stays false until the next `AudioSinkWrapper::Start()` ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#461)). Thus the stream never opens on the new device, and pause and resume do not help.
4. A seek stops and starts the media sink again. `AudioSinkWrapper::Start()` creates a new promise holder, so the new stream opens on the earbuds ([AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#418)). A reload has the same effect.

The periodic retry came from bug 1829054. It covers only a device that `setSinkId()` selected, not a new default device that appears during playback.

**Next steps**

When the default device fails and the media has video, we recommend to schedule a retry and keep the promise pending. Reject the promise only for media without video, so that audio-only playback can still stop with an error. The end-of-playback check must continue to work while the audio promise stays pending.

This bug now blocks the Bluetooth meta bug 2011679. We suggest that a developer sets the status to NEW.

No action is needed from you. As a workaround, seek or reload the tab after the earbuds connect.

comment:
Thank you for the clear steps.

**Analysis**

This looks like a gap in how Firefox recovers when playback starts with no audio output device. Firefox does not try again to open the audio stream on the default device.

When the audio stream cannot open, [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#665) tries again only for a device that the page selected with `setSinkId()`. For the default device, it rejects the ended promise and stops the audio sink. Then [MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/MediaDecoderStateMachine.cpp#4675) continues the video on the system clock without audio. Nothing opens the audio stream again when a new device connects.

Pause and resume do not help, because `NeedAudioSink()` in [AudioSinkWrapper.cpp](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/mediasink/AudioSinkWrapper.cpp#461) stays false after the reject. A seek stops and starts the audio sink again, so audio comes back on the new device. A reload or a new tab also makes a new audio sink. This behavior comes from the design in bug 1829054, so it is not a regression.

**Fix direction**

When the default device fails and the media has video, `AudioSinkWrapper` can schedule a retry and keep the ended promise. The existing retry in `GetPosition()` then opens the audio sink again after `media.audio.device.retry.ms` (1000 ms). A better trigger is the output device list event in [CubebDeviceEnumerator.h](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/416e49d66aacd49d5c51619e1b6d314e3961c8d7/dom/media/webrtc/CubebDeviceEnumerator.h#51). Audio-only media can keep the current error path.

**Next steps**

This bug now blocks bug 2011679, the meta bug for Bluetooth audio and video issues. A developer can start from the code above. No action is necessary from you. Until a fix lands, seek in the video or reload the tab to get the audio back.
